title: UK government updates guidance for domestic abuse victims abroad
excerpt: The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office provides information on support services and consular assistance for British citizens.
bodyHtml:
The UK government published updated guidance on November 6, 2026, regarding how British citizens can access help if they experience domestic abuse while abroad. The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) stated that consular staff can assist victims by providing information on local support services, helping contact family, and identifying English-speaking lawyers or medical facilities.

The guidance clarifies that while the FCDO can liaise with local authorities and banks, it cannot provide legal advice, collect evidence, or fund travel costs. Victims are advised to contact local emergency services if in immediate danger. In the European Union, the guidance notes that individuals should call 112 for emergency services.

The FCDO maintains a 24/7 support line in London at +44(0)20 7008 5000 for those requiring immediate information. Additionally, the National Domestic Abuse Helpline in the UK offers free, confidential advice and support to anyone experiencing domestic abuse and can be reached at 0808 2000 247.
